sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT EVERYDAY OCCURRENCES THE OTHER CALLER CONSIDERS TO BE AN INTRUSION OF PRIVACY.  WHAT CAN BE DONE TO PREVENT THEM?  DO YOU AGREE OR DISAGREE?
turns: Yeah, I totally get why that stuff gets annoying, actually. I was just in the ER yesterday and a guy walked in with a fever, and before I even asked his name, he started telling everyone in the waiting room his whole life story and where he lives. It felt like a violation, you know? Like, my job is to help him, not to listen to his childhood trauma while I'm trying to triage. But honestly, once I heard it, I felt like I could do a better job. What about you? Do you think hearing those details helps people, or does it just feel like an invasion?

Honestly, that's one thing I don't get, but then I tell my library patrons not to post their addresses on the door for mailers, and half of them just think I'm being weird or rude. It feels like breaking the ice, but it does feel like a breach to me.

Yeah, I get that about the library thing; it's weird when folks think keeping your address secret makes you snobby, but if people just don't want to be bothered, maybe putting a "No Solicitors" sign is the only fix?
Maybe, but honestly I've had people walk up to me and ask, "What's your building number?" before I even introduce myself, and it just feels creepy when they want to find you when you're not there.
Yeah, that's the scary part, it feels like they're hunting for you instead of trying to help. Maybe the only way to stop that is just not giving out your building number at all, even to librarians.
Yeah, I guess I'm just paranoid that if I don't put my name on the front door, some random person could just come knock on my door late at night and figure out who I am anyway.
Yeah, I see where you're coming from on the paranoia, but honestly, I'd rather risk the creepy knock than have a stranger wander into my apartment just because they saw my name on the door.
I mean, that's true, but then again, I lived in an old building where the mailman always knew exactly who was home and who wasn't, so maybe hiding the name doesn't work if they're already inside.

Yeah, that's the thing about old buildings though, you never know who's actually home or if the mailman's just trying to sell you something, which is why I'd rather just not give them a name to start with.
I guess you have a point, but it still feels like I'm inviting trouble just to keep my door closed. Do you ever have people try to find your house even though you're a nurse in a hospital?
I mean, never had anyone come to the hospital room looking for me specifically. Usually it's just patients asking for their meds or family members looking for a specific doctor, so it's different.
Yeah, that's a relief, because if people were showing up at the hospital asking for you, I'd probably be terrified you were getting targeted or stalked.
I guess you're right to be worried, but honestly my hospital is pretty secure, so I don't really have to worry about strangers tracking me down there.

Yeah, that security stuff makes me feel better, but sometimes it still feels like the system is designed to keep people *out* rather than keep my data private, which is a weird thing to think about when you're helping folks.

Yeah, but that's where it gets tricky for me too, because sometimes you need a little bit of info to actually help someone, so I guess I try to balance being careful without locking myself off from doing my job right.

Yeah, I get that part about needing info to help, but sometimes it feels like the line blurs too much, like if a patient just says "my sister lives on 4th" I shouldn't have to look up the whole block.
Yeah, I get that, but usually patients don't say that stuff unless they're looking for a specific person, and I just tell them I can't check without a name so they know I'm not just guessing around.

Yeah, that's fair, but I still think it's a little weird when people ask for info just to see if you're busy or not, even if they say they're family. Like, why can't they just call your cell phone or leave a voicemail instead of coming straight to the unit? It feels like they're trying to catch you off guard.
Yeah, and honestly it's just annoying when folks assume I'm ignoring them, but maybe if they waited for me to step out or call back, it wouldn't feel like an ambush.
Yeah, that's a fair point, but sometimes they just won't leave a message and stand there in the hallway staring at you while you try to grab a chart.
Yeah, at least you don't have to sit there for twenty minutes while they stare, I usually just tell them to hold or leave a message if I'm in the middle of a chart and they keep asking.
Yeah, that's the worst part, just standing there while you try to pull up records, it feels like they're trying to figure out if you're gonna answer the phone or not.

Yeah, I usually just tell them to hold or leave a message if I'm in the middle of a chart and they keep asking, but honestly, once in a while I'll just let them in if I'm not too busy, because it feels wrong to just shut the door on someone standing there.
Yeah, I guess that's just how people are, but honestly, most of the time I just tell them to hold and say I'll get to them, even if it feels a little rude.

Yeah, I know, and sometimes I just let them in if I'm not too busy, but honestly, once in a while I'll just let them in if I'm not too busy, because it feels wrong to just shut the door on someone standing there.

Yeah, I guess it is, but sometimes those folks just won't go away until you give them the answer, even if it's just a different ward or unit, so I do feel like I'm getting dragged into their business a little bit.
Yeah, I guess you're right, and honestly I probably should just tell them to leave a message and close the door before I even get annoyed.

Yeah, but sometimes that "just leave a message" thing feels like they're gonna stand there until I actually give them the room number anyway, so I end up just telling them which floor it is and telling them to go look it up themselves.
Yeah, I guess that's the worst part, knowing you're stuck in the middle just so they can fish for the rest of the details themselves.
Yeah, it's just like giving someone a map to your house when you don't even want them to know you live there anymore.
Yeah, it's like handing someone a key without asking if they're even a guest first.
Yeah, except sometimes the map turns out to be exactly what I wanted to avoid, like they end up knocking on my neighbor's door anyway.
Yeah, and honestly that's the worst part—just knowing someone has the floor number is basically handing them a key without even asking if they're a guest first.
That's exactly why I keep my door closed tight and never look them in the eye when they start asking.
Yeah, it's just that feeling of being totally exposed even if you think you've locked everything down.
Yeah, but sometimes people just won't stop asking until they find your door, so it feels like I'm just giving up my whole street to keep them from knowing my name.
Yeah, honestly it just feels like I'm opening up the windows for strangers just to keep them out of my name.
Yeah, maybe I should just leave the door closed forever and hope they eventually give up.
Yeah, maybe you just leave the door locked and hope they eventually get the hint and walk away.
Yeah, I'll try that, but honestly, sometimes they just won't stop knocking until they get an answer.
